papers.title: $\mathrm{v}$-numbers of powers of edge ideals of cubic circulant graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide the exact formula for the $\mathrm{v}$-number of powers of the edge ideal of a cubic circulant graph $C_{2n}(a,n)$ with $1\le a<n$.

papers.title: On Hankel Determinantal Matroids
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of the algebraic matroid associated to the ideal generated by the $(r+1)$-minors of a Hankel matrix of variables. We prove that this matroid is uniform, that is, a coordinate projection from the corresponding Hankel determinantal variety is generically finite if and only if it preserves at least $2r$ anti-diagonals. For such projections, we establish bounds on the degree. These results are of significance to the problem of Hankel low-rank matrix completion.

papers.title: On the Fluctuations of Associated Primes and Depths of Powers of Monomial Ideals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the fluctuation phenomenon in the sets of associated primes and depths of powers of monomial ideals. We provide affirmative answers to two open questions posed in [8] concerning the existence of monomial ideals in K[x,y,z] whose associated primes exhibit prescribed patterns of appearance, disappearance, and reappearance of the maximal ideal across specified ranges of powers. For each construction, we also derive the corresponding fluctuation in depths. Furthermore, we construct a square-free monomial ideal that is nearly normally torsion-free but fails to satisfy the persistence property, thereby answering a question posed in [20] in the negative. This example arises as the edge ideal of the ideal minimally non-packing clutter Q_10, revealing an intriguing connection between combinatorial optimization and the algebraic properties of monomial ideals.

papers.title: Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function. A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs. Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.

papers.title: The theory of F-rational signature
papers.abstract: F-signature is an important numeric invariant of singularities in positive characteristic that can be used to detect strong F-regularity. One would like to have a variant that rather detects F-rationality, and there are two theories that aim to fill this gap: F-rational signature of Hochster and Yao and dual F-signature of Sannai. Unfortunately, several important properties of the original F-signature are unknown for these invariants. We give a modification of the Hochster-Yao definition that agrees with Sannai's dual F-signature and push further the united theory to achieve a complete generalization of F-signature.

papers.title: Descent problem for certificate of non-negativity on semi-algebraic sets
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a subfield of $\mathbb R$ and let $K$ be a basic closed semi-algebraic set in $\mathbb R$ with $\partial K\subset F$. Let $\mathcal N$ be the natural choice of generators of $K$. We show that if $f\in F[x]$ is $\geq 0$ on $K$, then $f$ can be written as $$f=\sum_{e\in\{0,1\}^s } a_e\sigma_e g^e $$ where $a_e\in F_{\geq 0}$, $\sigma_e\in \sum F[x]^2$ and $g^{e}=g_1^{e_1} \cdots g_s^{e_s}$. In other words, the preordering $T_{\mathcal N}$ of $F[x]$ is saturated. In case $F=\mathbb R$, this result is due to Kuhlmann and Marshall. As an application, we prove that if $K$ is compact, then $M_{\mathcal N}=T_{\mathcal N}=Pos(K)$. In other words, the quadratic module $M_{\mathcal N}$ of $F[x]$ is saturated.

papers.title: Ramification ideals for products of pure subgroups
papers.abstract: We study ramification ideals of finite Galois extensions of henselian valued fields whose Galois groups are products of pure subgroups. We give a criterion showing that the ideals supplied by the factors need not exhaust all subgroup ideals, and construct $C_p^2$-counterexamples of rank one with each defect $1,p,p^2$. For ramification-adapted families, whose intersections generate each ramification group, every subgroup ideal is represented by a cyclic subgroup of one member; when the members are pure, this gives a description in terms of distance sets. Such adapted decompositions always exist for elementary abelian groups. We also characterize principality of ramification ideals through defectlessness of the pure adapted factors. Kuhlmann's example shows that these conditions do not imply defectlessness of the full extension.

papers.title: Point Counts of Cluster Varieties of Marked Surfaces Over Finite Fields
papers.abstract: We establish formulae for point counts of cluster varieties of cluster algebras of marked surfaces, possibly with punctures. We then establish formulae for the number of non-deep points in these cluster varieties over $\mathbb{F}_2$, which gives us the number of algebraic tori necessary to cover the cluster manifold over $\mathbb{F}_2$. We also show that these formulae satisfy certain recurrence relations.

papers.title: Generalizing Green's Syzygy Theorems to Symmetric Products of Curves
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$, and let $T_{n,L}$ denote the tautological line bundle on its $n$-th symmetric product $C_n$. We prove effective vanishing criteria for Koszul cohomology $K_{p,q}(C_n,T_{n,B};T_{n,L})$, extending two classical theorems of Mark Green. The main ingredient is a weight-one vanishing theorem proved by induction on $n$, using a filtration of the kernel bundle of $T_{n,L}$ to reduce the required cohomological vanishings to lower symmetric products. As a consequence, when $g\geq1$ and $n\geq2$, $T_{n,L}$ satisfies property $(N_p)$ for $\mathrm{deg}(L)\geq(n+1)g+p$. This bound is sharp for elliptic symmetric squares and also gives evidence for a folklore conjecture on adjoint syzygies.

papers.title: Commutative rings with square-difference factor absorbing factorization
papers.abstract: We introduce and study sdf-absorbing factorization rings (SAF-rings), in which every regular ideal is a finite product of square-difference factor absorbing ideals. We investigate their behavior under direct products, localizations, factor rings, and module idealizations, and establish connections with SP-rings, Dedekind rings, and N-rings. We also introduce strongly sdf-absorbing factorization rings (SSAF-rings), relate them to SSP-rings and almost multiplication rings, and prove that the Noetherian SSAF-rings are precisely the ZPI-rings. Applications to module idealizations and monoid rings are also presented.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of I. Chowla's Theorem on Addition of Residue Classes
papers.abstract: We present a brief, elementary proof of a striking theorem by I. Chowla on the addition of residue classes (1937) which generalizes the famous result of Cauchy and Davenport to residue classes modulo a composite.
